original_question: Does every subgroup of a virtually polycyclic group have bounded packing, meaning that for every radius r > 0 there exists N such that any collection of N distinct left cosets contains two cosets whose distance is at least r with respect to a proper left-invariant metric on the ambient group?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1: every subgroup of a virtually polycyclic group has the bounded packing property.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s target: it has the right ambient class (virtually polycyclic groups), the right property (bounded packing), the correct universal quantifier over subgroups, and the standard metric formulation with 'for every r > 0 there exists N' for collections of distinct left cosets.
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, the subgroup should be named explicitly: for every virtually polycyclic group P and every subgroup H ≤ P.
The paper’s formal definition uses the distance between left H-cosets gH and g'H, so the coset distance should be specified as d(gH, g'H) = inf{d(x,y) : x ∈ gH, y ∈ g'H}.
The metric should be stated as any proper left-invariant metric on the ambient group; the paper also notes that bounded packing is independent of the choice of such metric.
To match the paper exactly, the problem should be framed as the bounded packing property of subgroups, not just an informal distance condition.

The nearby context includes an equivalent reformulation (Proposition 1.2) reducing the conjecture from virtually polycyclic groups to polycyclic groups; your draft does not mention that paper-explicit equivalence.

If one wants to situate the question relative to the paper’s proved results, the paper’s positive evidence is the special case of diagonal semidirect products Z^n ⋊_φ Z with φ diagonalizable and all eigenvalues real, yielding polycyclic groups of length at most 3; your draft does not indicate that narrower proved scope.
refined_question: Conjecture. For every virtually polycyclic group P and every subgroup H ≤ P, does H have the bounded packing property in P? Equivalently: for every proper left-invariant metric d on P and every r > 0, does there exist N = N(P,H,r) such that any collection of N distinct left H-cosets in P contains two cosets gH and g'H with d(gH,g'H) ≥ r, where d(gH,g'H) := inf{d(x,y) : x ∈ gH, y ∈ g'H}?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalent formulation from Proposition 1.2: Does every subgroup of every polycyclic group have bounded packing?
justification: The draft is targeting the paper’s central bounded-packing conjecture rather than one of its later special-case theorems. The surrounding discussion introduces bounded packing in the metric form you used, then singles out the virtually polycyclic case as the conjectural target. The paper also highlights an equivalent reduction to the polycyclic case, and its later proved special case is that certain semidirect products Z^n ⋊_φ Z have bounded packing for all subgroups, from which the length-at-most-3 polycyclic case follows.
